messages.subject: Model extention and trial-level regressor in LBA
messages.subject_clean: Model extention and trial-level regressor in LBA
messages.body_plain:
First of all, sorry for overflooding the forum with my issues with the LBA model. However, with help from the forum I did figure many things out and  can share some code that might help someone in the future.

 In particular, I was able to:

- extend the stan model to fit varying non-decision times per condition. The extention can also quite easily be modified to accommodate different thresholds per condition.
- simulate posterior predictive from individual parameters using r rtdists package (I believe the original function is supposed to provide this functionality, however the output seems ambiguous; see related post).

If anyone is interested in these, I'll be happy to share.

Having that out of the way, I am trying to fit a trial-level EEG regressor to the model and having trouble doing so. I've read the post about applying subject-level regressors in a different task but struggle to translate this into single-trial regressors in LBA. Could anyone provide a guideline how I should go about it?

Best,
Wojciech

messages.subject_clean: Model extention and trial-level regressor in LBA
messages.body_plain:
Hi Wojciech,

One of our plans for a future release is to make the DDM (among other models) more flexible for looking at between-condition effects, but I am not sure when exactly that will happen. That said, it would be great if you could share your extension here—I am sure that other users would benefit from it greatly.

For non-learning tasks, the concept of trial-by-trial regressors is a bit different. This is because there are no latent terms in the model that we can easily extract. However, there are examples of people creating trail-by-trial drift rates and such, which is similar to estimating a trial-level drift rate (see references below). I have never actually coded one of these up in Stan, but I am sure there is a way to do it.

References:

van Maanen, L., Brown, S. D., Eichele, T., Wagenmakers, E. J., Ho, T., Serences, J., & Forstmann, B. U. (2011). Neural correlates of trial-to-trial fluctuations in response caution. Journal of Neuroscience, 31(48), 17488-17495.

Rodriguez, C. A., Turner, B. M., Van Zandt, T., and McClure, S. M. (2015). The neural basis of value accumulation in intertemporal choice. European JoN. 1-11.

messages.subject: LBA extensions thread
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm making a separate thread for extensions to the LBA model. Since I'm doing a lot of fiddling with the model, I thought it would be productive to share the code. Unfortunately, running the models takes very long on my current equipment, so I am unable to test all of these (I am testing only those that are relevant to my current project). All the extensions are made for the group-level LBA estimation (choiceRT_lba.R), and NOT for the individual one (choiceRT_lba_single.R) I will do my best to update this thread.

TESTED means I tested parameter recovery of the model. UNTESTED means I either run the individual model without testing recovery accuracy, or just wrote the code without running it (in that case the code might contain some unexpected syntax errors).

Please feel free to incorporate these to the package or use these individually (but be sure to first test parameter recovery of the untested models).

1. Allowing different parameters to vary per condition.
 To run these STAN files one needs to adjust 'modelPath' in the R function 'choiceRT_lba.R'

 - separate T0 (non-decision times) per condition (DONE, TESTED); file: choiceRT_lba_t.stan
 - separate A (starting-point variability) per condition (DONE, UNTESTED); file: choiceRT_lba_A.stan
 - separate d (boudary - A) per condition  (DONE, UNTESTED); file: choiceRT_lba_d.stan
 - separate A & d per condition (DONE, UNTESTED); file: choiceRT_lba_Ad.stan
 - separate A & T0 per condition (DONE, UNTESTED); file: choiceRT_lba_At.stan
 - separate d & T0 per condition (DONE, UNTESTED); file: choiceRT_lba_dt.stan
 - separate A, d  & T0 per condition (DONE, UNTESTED); file: choiceRT_lba_Adt.stan

2. Fixing Decision Boundary (A+d) instead of drift-rate variability (s)
To run these in addition to 'modelPath' one needs to adjust the estimated parameters as well in the R function

 -  IN PREPARATION

3. Adding trial-based model regressors
- IN PREPARATION

4. Adjusting the choiceRT_lba.R function to accommodate all the models
- when everything else is ready

Additionally, things I'll maybe add given enough time:

5. Adding individual regressors (i.e. some individual difference measures)

6. R function (or a set of functions) to generate posterior predictive estimates (simulated data given individual model parameters using rtdists package)
This might not be needed, as this functionality is already implemented, but I honestly don't know whether it works correctly, as I get very weird estimated when trying to use it (refer to the forum thread about posterior predictive in LBA).

Best,
Wojciech

Hi Matt,

Thanks for contacting us! At this point, I think it would be most ideal if you send us some required files and we will add the model to hBayesDM.

Minimum required files include a Stan file, its example data (*.txt file), its reference, and a list of model parameters and their parameter bounds (e.g., learning rate —> between 0 and 1).

We plan to make the package more modular to make it easier to add new models.

Best,
Young

messages.subject: Repeated measures, within-subject condition comparison
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

For a new study we performed using a reinforcement learning task, I would like to try the hBayesDM toolboox for model fitting, comparison, and parameter comparinson, The set-up of my study however makes me doubt about the approach I should take. This is a more conceptual problem in the context of hierarchical Bayes models, which might have practical consequences on how to proceed:
Our dataset exists of a repeated measures design: one intervention, one placebo condition within subjects, counterbalanced. We assessed the task during both conditions. So I have two datafiles per person. I want to know if parameters during intervention differ from parameters during placebo.
As the hierarchical Bayes takes the group mean into account, I wonder if I should fit all the data in one go (with the risk that both conditions regress to the mean, removing possible variance), or if I should model the two conditions separately (with the risk to inflate possible differences between conditions).

What would be wisdom here? I guess my main concern is how hBayesDM handles within-subject versus between-subject error and related (in)dependencies.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Repeated measures, within-subject condition comparison
messages.body_plain:
Hi  - this is a good question.

I would start with fitting data from the placebo condition first, which sets the baseline.
Then, you could use the posterior from the placebo condition as the prior for the treatment condition, which tests how your treatment shifts the parameter.
For modify the priors, go to R-3.x.x/library/hBayesDM/stan.

I would also be curious about how Young and others will deal with this problem.

Hope it helps.
L.

---
Lei Zhang

messages.subject: Re: Repeated measures, within-subject condition comparison
messages.body_plain:
Definitely a good question.

My way of approaching this in the past has been to create a difference variable that estimates the difference between conditions. Another way to think about it is to estimate a different parameter for each condition.

To find out which (if any) parameters are affected by the manipulation, I fit various models that assume either no differences, difference in only parameter X, difference in only parameter Y, etc., and then I use model comparison to select the best model.

Unfortunately, hBayesDM is not able to estimate within-subject parameter differences in its current state, so you would have to modify the stan code to do so. This is a feature that would be great to add in the future.

Best,
Nate
From: hbayesd...@googlegroups.com <hbayesd...@googlegroups.com> on behalf of Zsuzsika Sjoerds <sjoer...@gmail.com>
Sent: Tuesday, September 18, 2018 7:17:00 AM
To: hbayesdm-users
Subject: Repeated measures, within-subject condition comparison

Hi all,

For a new study we performed using a reinforcement learning task, I would like to try the hBayesDM toolboox for model fitting, comparison, and parameter comparinson, The set-up of my study however makes me doubt about the approach I should take. This is a more conceptual problem in the context of hierarchical Bayes models, which might have practical consequences on how to proceed:
Our dataset exists of a repeated measures design: one intervention, one placebo condition within subjects, counterbalanced. We assessed the task during both conditions. So I have two datafiles per person. I want to know if parameters during intervention differ from parameters during placebo.
As the hierarchical Bayes takes the group mean into account, I wonder if I should fit all the data in one go (with the risk that both conditions regress to the mean, removing possible variance), or if I should model the two conditions separately (with the risk to inflate possible differences between conditions).

What would be wisdom here? I guess my main concern is how hBayesDM handles within-subject versus between-subject error and related (in)dependencies.

Thanks!

--
